subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what security guarantee should it make across top-level navigations, redirects, subframes/subresources, and proxy-routed browser profiles?
rationale: The request adds operator-trusted browser security/config semantics that current SSRF hostname allowlists do not define, so automation should not choose the permanent policy boundary.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the browser-scoped deny/warn semantics, then implement the schema, guard, docs, and tests against that contract.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Make the related generic egress-firewall work own browser navigation too, but only after it explicitly covers browser redirects, proxy, and subresource behavior.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable denylist and instead document or surface best-effort bot-blocked-site warnings that do not claim to be a security boundary.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the browser-scoped deny/warn semantics, then implement the schema, guard, docs, and tests against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the strongest routing candidate from adjacent browser SSRF/config and current web egress policy history.
